a single word that arrives late and rearranges the line before it
the poem insists on a silence where the reader expects a statement
one image drawn from the body — the hand, the breath, the ache — anchors the whole
the light changes mid-poem: day to night, lamp to dawn, and the mood follows
a repeated sound the speaker cannot stop returning to
the last line refuses the consolation the rest of the poem was building
a small, concrete object stands in for the whole burden without being explained
the meter breaks exactly where the grief does
the speaker addresses someone who is no longer there, and is not answered
the poem ends on a question it has no right to ask
